Please read /papers/investigations-5/01_heat_density_asymptotics/research-progress/handoffs/HDA-17-AN05.md, and the research overview /01_heat_density_asymptotics/research-overview/01_AVERAGED_DENSITY_RESEARCH_PROGRAM_20261024.md

Continue HDA-17-AN05 r1: prove the positive-source compression and complete cost bound, or identify the first unpaid analytical estimate.

Track your progress in the research progress folder, write research notes in the notes folder, and record chat history in the chat-histories folder.
I’ll read the handoff, overview, and repository instructions, then work through the compression and cost argument, recording the proof or first missing estimate in the investigation folders.

Note55 already supplies the absolute four-jet target. The compression route first needs a complex zero-free region for the full source; positivity on the real axis alone does not provide one. I’m checking that branch bound and the approximation cost in parallel, within the packet’s analytical-only scope.

The branch estimate closes: the full source has a positive analytic square root on an explicit strip of width \(1/16\), with a norm bound independent of the cutoff. This supports geometric polynomial approximation. I’m now paying the coefficient and rounding costs, especially the absolute square-root accuracy needed where the source is tiny.

The source ledger now closes. At fixed upper time, the specified source descriptor uses \(O(R^2\log R)\) bits for the same four-jet target, replacing Note55’s exponential upper bound. The argument includes node construction, all omitted-mode errors, rounding, exact conversion, and a finite construction cost bound. I’m checking and saving it; accurate Gaussian-moment evaluation and continuous filtering remain open.

Note58 and Review37 are saved, and the existing handoff and progress register are updated. The internal analytical checks found no unpaid source-stage estimate; file and link checks passed. I’m finishing the chat-history capture. Evaluator precision and continuous filtering remain the next work for Sol.

Completed AN05 r1 at analytical source-construction scope in [Note58](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/investigations-5/01_heat_density_asymptotics/notes/58_POSITIVE_ANALYTIC_SOURCE_COMPRESSION_20261025.md).

The proof supplies:

- An explicit complex square-root branch for the complete canonical source.
- A nonnegative polynomial source with four-jet error \(\le51\epsilon/256\).
- Full coefficient, rounding, mode, tail and construction-cost payments.
- Source storage \(O_b(R^2\log R)\) bits at fixed upper time, replacing the previous exponential upper bound.

The first unpaid estimate is now **evaluator working precision**, followed by observable arithmetic and continuous filtering. **Analysis — Sol** is the next owner.

Progress, handoff, internal assessment and chat history are updated. No research computations were run. HDA-17 remains Partial, HDA-18 Gated, and HDA-20 unfulfilled; review is same-model only.

Please continue analytically with Note58’s evaluator working-precision and continuous-filter error ledger for the unchanged IC23 tuple. Save progress, research notes, and chat history in the investigation folders.

I’ll use Note58’s source and the unchanged IC23 targets to derive the evaluator and continuous-filter error ledger, stopping at the first unpaid estimate if it does not close. I’ll save the analysis and progress in the investigation folders and refresh this chat’s history.

The source field remains active at every real height during the early part of the joined construction, so a bounded-core evaluator would not cover the full request. The moment evaluator can retain that scope with an explicit cost depending on the query height. I’m also tracing the regulator, saddle and filter inputs needed for the full observable tuple.

The source evaluator has a cancellation-safe route: evaluate the moments by a convergent series and exact rational sums, with separate bounds for truncation, coordinates and rounding. The filter rule also has a finite error bound. One upstream issue remains: evaluating an already fixed phase index is covered, but constructing its literal ceiling from scratch needs an equality or separation argument not supplied by the current estimates. I’ll record that distinction.

The ledger is ready to save. It pays source and auxiliary-field evaluation from a certified descriptor, continuous filtering, actual covariance, and all retained defects. The bounds are finite but can be very expensive; they establish no useful runtime yet. The exact phase-index ceiling remains the first unpaid step in constructing the descriptor from scratch.

Note59 and Review38 are saved, and the progress register is synchronized. The file and link checks passed; no research calculations were run. I’m finishing the chat-history capture. The recorded next gate is exact phase-index construction, separate from the remaining useful-cost work.

Saved [Note59](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/investigations-5/01_heat_density_asymptotics/notes/59_EVALUATOR_WORKING_PRECISION_AND_CONTINUOUS_FILTER_20261025.md) with working-bit bounds and a continuous-filter error ledger for the unchanged IC23 tuple, including actual covariance and every defect.

The theorem assumes certified descriptor data, including the exact phase index \(n\). The first unpaid construction step is deciding the literal ceiling \(n=\lceil\Theta(64,2^k)/\pi\rceil\); the existing estimates supply no terminating equality/separation rule.

The bounds can be prohibitively expensive. Review38 is same-model internal assessment; no research computations were run. Progress and chat history are updated, with final-reply capture arranged.

**Next: Analysis — Sol**, exact phase-index construction and useful-cost improvements. HDA-17/18/20 statuses remain unchanged.

Please continue analytically with Note59’s exact phase-index construction for the unchanged IC23 tuple. Resolve the ceiling/equality issue, and save progress, research notes, and chat history in the investigation folders.

I’ll trace the exact phase-index rule and check whether the ceiling can be decided for the existing tuple. I’ll save the argument—or the precise unresolved step—in the investigation folders and refresh this chat’s history.

Does “unchanged IC23 tuple” fix a particular onset exponent k, or may I use Note54’s existing freedom to choose a sufficiently large binary onset? A four-onset construction may avoid equality while preserving the literal ceiling rule and all IC23 formulas; it would not recover an already fixed k.
- Use existing onset freedom
- Keep a particular k fixed

I’ll use the existing onset freedom. The analytical route is promising: a combination of the phases at four consecutive binary onsets cancels the leading terms and stays strictly between integers. That gives a separated candidate on which the original ceiling rule can be decided, without needing to decide equality at every candidate.

The four-onset argument closes the equality issue within the authorized scope. At least one candidate has phase distance greater than \(1/100\) from every integer; a finite rational calculation can identify a safe candidate and its exact ceiling. I’m recording the proof and cost bound, while preserving the distinction from the still-open problem at an arbitrarily fixed onset.

The proof also pays for the precision needed to identify the winner: although the acceptance margin is fixed, the large phase requires a number of accuracy bits proportional to the onset exponent. The selector has a polynomial bit bound in that exponent. The remaining cost issue is in Note59’s continuous-filter estimates and auxiliary evaluators; HDA-17 and HDA-18 retain their current statuses.

Note60, its internal assessment, and the progress updates are saved. I’m checking the links and status records, then refreshing this chat’s existing history. The recorded scope is explicit: the literal ceiling is constructed using the permitted onset freedom; useful complete runtime remains open, and no research computation was executed.

Resolved using the authorized onset freedom. [Note60](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/investigations-5/01_heat_density_asymptotics/notes/60_EXACT_PHASE_INDEX_BY_DYADIC_ONSET_SELECTION_20261025.md) proves that one of four admissible binary onsets has phase distance \(>1/100\) from every integer. Finite rational tests identify a winner and its **literal exact ceiling**, with polynomial selector cost in the onset exponent.

All IC23 formulas remain unchanged. Equality at an arbitrary previously fixed onset remains outside this result.

Research notes, assessment and [progress](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/investigations-5/01_heat_density_asymptotics/research-progress/01_AVERAGED_DENSITY_RESEARCH_PROGRESS_20261024.md) are saved. Chat history is refreshed, with final-reply capture arranged. No research computations ran.

**Next: Analysis — Sol**, improving the complete evaluator/filter cost. HDA-17 Partial, HDA-18 Gated and HDA-20 unfulfilled remain.
Ok please continue with improving the complete evaluator/filter cost, and then write a summary of all of the research in this chat

I’ll continue from Note60 by looking for a carrier-aware estimate that reduces Note59’s evaluator and filtering cost while retaining the complete IC23 tuple. Then I’ll write a summary of this chat’s research and save both results in the investigation folders.

There is a concrete improvement available: the inherited smoothness bounds support a higher-order rational quadrature rule whose cost grows polynomially in the requested accuracy bits, for a fixed descriptor and query box. That would remove Note59’s exponential dependence on accuracy from midpoint integration. I’m also checking faster gamma and profile evaluators, and whether the separate dependence on height can be reduced.

The accuracy-bit improvement now covers the complete retained tuple, including direct time rows, actual covariance, and every joining defect. A separate height-cost issue remains: raw density has narrow peaks near zeros. The existing weak identities suggest how to integrate around those peaks, but that route still needs a complete quadrature ledger.

The analytical continuation and whole-chat summary are drafted. Review caught an important scope point: an arbitrary computable fixed scalar can have expensive digits, so its provider cost must stay explicit. The polynomial bound applies to the stated rational/dyadic inputs and canonical recipes; the general bound carries external scalar costs. I’m saving that qualification with the proof and summary.

Saved Note61 and the full chat summary, Note62. The new result improves accuracy-bit cost for the complete tuple at the stated fixed-data scope. The remaining estimate is now specific: a complete weak-filter error and cost ledger with collar guards, actual mean products, and coordinate error bounds. Prior notes are preserved, and the saved links and input hashes check out.

[Note61](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/investigations-5/01_heat_density_asymptotics/notes/61_POLYNOMIAL_ACCURACY_EVALUATOR_AND_FILTER_COST_20261025.md) now proves **polynomial accuracy-bit cost for the complete evaluator/filter**, at fixed descriptor and query box with the stated scalar encodings. General scalar-provider costs remain explicit.

The [whole-chat summary, Note62](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/investigations-5/01_heat_density_asymptotics/notes/62_CHAT0021_RESEARCH_SUMMARY_20261025.md), records four results:

- Positive source compression with a complete four-jet and construction-cost bound.
- Working-precision, arithmetic and continuous-filter error estimates.
- Exact phase-ceiling construction using the authorized onset freedom.
- Improved accuracy-bit cost through efficient providers and higher-order quadrature.

**Useful uniform height cost remains open.** The next estimate is the complete weak-filter cost bound, including collar guards, actual mean products and coordinate error bounds.

Progress, assessment, research notes and chat history are saved. No research computations ran. HDA-17 remains Partial, HDA-18 Gated and HDA-20 unfulfilled.
